Traupman 353

vetus, veteris

adjective, third declension, one ending; comparative vetustior

The everyday opposite of novus: old things, an old friend (vetus amīcus), an old soldier. Of an old person it means one of long standing; for aged people the word is senex (see old, of people).

Other words

  • vetustus, vetusta, vetustum — old, of long standing

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. vetustus

    Old because it has lasted a long time: an old house, an old custom.

  • antīquus, antīqua, antīquum — old, of former times

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. antīquus

    Old as belonging to the past, “old-time”, “ancient”; for a worn object say vetus.

Examples

  • bovēs vetulōs, plōstrum vetus, ferrāmenta vetera, servum senem

    (let him sell) the old oxen, the old cart, the old tools, the old slaveCato Agr. 2.7 (Lewis & Short)

See also new, old.
